comment: The run chain: the ordered stages that build this project from nothing to a verified demo. Derived from the milestones M0-M6 in docs/PLAN.md. Each stage names its owner agent, what it must deliver, and the checks that prove it is done. tools/chain.mjs runs the checks, reports status, and prints a brief for the next unfinished stage. Commands run from the repo root.

stages.title: Toolchain installed
stages.goal: Arm GNU Toolchain and QEMU are installed and reachable by firmware/build.mjs (default paths, or ARM_TOOLCHAIN_BIN / QEMU_BIN).

stages.title: A429 codec and golden vectors
stages.goal: Bit-exact ARINC 429 encode/decode in JS, pinned by golden vectors derived twice.

stages.title: Firmware builds and its words decode correctly
stages.goal: Bare-metal Cortex-M3 image for QEMU mps2-an385 that parses pad frames on UART1 and emits six A429 words per 50 Hz tick on UART0.

stages.title: Pad reader streams the real gamepad
stages.manual: Move each stick and press each button; the live table must show the matching parameter change.
stages.goal: host/pad-reader.ps1 reads the gamepad (HID, WinMM fallback) and streams 17-byte frames at 50 Hz to QEMU.

stages.title: Backend decodes, converts and judges freshness
stages.goal: ParamState with watchdog and resync, DisplayConfig, HTTP + SSE server, live and replay ingest.

stages.title: SFD and config pages
stages.manual: Open /sfd and /config with `node tools/run-all.mjs --replay`; move a slider and see the SFD scale follow; check the STALE/NCD flags.
stages.goal: Secondary Flight Display and one slider set per parameter, fed by SSE, with full validity flags.

stages.title: End to end and decoupled replay
stages.goal: Live TCP ingest reaches the browser; the backend replays a real capture with QEMU and the pad absent.

stages.title: Measured 50 Hz
stages.goal: The firmware's real word rate is about 50 Hz, measured, not inferred.

stages.title: AI framework and pipeline consistent
stages.goal: Rules, agents, skills, ownership and Claude Code wrappers agree with the code; CI runs the chain.
